answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with refundable stake deposits bound to a reputation graph. Every identity must lock capital at the vertex where it joins the network, and that stake is slashed when peers detect coordinated fake behavior. Forging a thousand agents means locking a thousand deposits, each as hard and unyielding as onyx, so a swarm stops being a cheap island of puppets and becomes an expensive fleet whose potential loss grows faster than any reward it could extract.
